chunks: And it is narrated from Ibrāhīm ibn Abī Ziyād al-Karkhī that he said:
I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: An elderly old man is unable, due to his weakness, to rise for relieving himself, and he is not able to perform rukūʿ or sujūd.

He عليه السلام said: He should gesture with his head as an indication, and if he has someone who can raise the khumrah up to him, then he should perform sajdah. But if that is not possible for him, then he should gesture with his head toward the qiblah as an indication.

I said: And fasting? He عليه السلام said: If he has reached that limit, then Allah has lifted it from him. If he has some ability, then giving charity of one mudd of food in place of each day is more beloved to me. But if he does not have the means for that, then there is nothing upon him.

key_terms.الْخُمْرَةَ: a small mat or surface used for prostration

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for an elderly sick person who cannot perform rukūʿ, sujūd, or fasting?
ai.summary: This hadith gives legal rulings for an elderly and severely weakened person who cannot perform the normal actions of salat or observe sawm. It teaches that such a person prays by head gestures when necessary, and that fasting is lifted when incapacity reaches this level, while charity in place of each missed day is preferred if he is able.
